mechanism_of_action.value: Piperacillin is a semisynthetic penicillin that exerts bactericidal activity by inhibiting septum formation and cell wall synthesis of susceptible bacteria. Tazobactam is a penicillanic acid sulfone beta-lactamase inhibitor of Molecular class A enzymes (Richmond-Sykes class III / Bush class 2b and 2b' penicillinases and cephalosporinases) that protects piperacillin from beta-lactamase hydrolysis.

refs.quote: Piperacillin sodium exerts bactericidal activity by inhibiting septum formation and cell wall synthesis of susceptible bacteria.
It is, however, a beta-lactamase inhibitor of the Molecular class A enzymes, including Richmond-Sykes class III (Bush class 2b & 2b') penicillinases and cephalosporinases.

Piperacillin is metabolized to a minor microbiologically active desethyl metabolite. Tazobactam is metabolized to a single metabolite that lacks pharmacological and antibacterial activities. value.effect: Prolongs half-life of piperacillin by 21% and tazobactam by 71% by inhibiting renal tubular secretion.
value.management: Should not be co-administered with ZOSYN unless the benefit outweighs the risk.
